title: The Raccoon and the Grumpy Cloud

pages.text: This is {name}. {name} is a fluffy little raccoon with a dark mask around bright eyes and quick, clever paws. Home is a cozy burrow under an old oak tree, right at the edge of a sunny forest clearing.
Today {name} has a grand plan: a pebble tower! Down by the stream the pebbles are round and smooth and warm from the sun. {name} scoops up a whole pawful — click, clack, click.
One pebble, two pebbles, three... {name} stacks them oh-so-carefully, tongue tip poking out with the effort. The tower grows taller than a dandelion!
Wibble-wobble — down it tumbles! The pebbles roll off in every direction. {name} sighs, picks them up, and starts again. Oh well, these things happen.
The tower falls a second time, right in front of that little black nose. {name} frowns. Now the paws are stacking faster — and grumpier.
And then — a third time! The pebbles bounce into the grass like little grasshoppers. {name} stomps a paw — STOMP! — and suddenly a small grumpy cloud appears right above that furry head.
The cloud is grey and scruffy, with cross little eyebrows. {name} stomps again — stomp-stomp! — and the cloud grows a bit bigger. Uh-oh.
{name} shouts at the cloud: "Go away!" But shouting only makes the cloud darker, and it grumbles right back: rumble-rumble-rumble.
{name} hides under a big burdock leaf and peeks out ever so quietly. But there is the cloud — hovering right above the leaf, darker than ever.
{name} runs around the clearing — fast, fast, fast! The cloud flies right behind, as if tied on with a string. Plip! — down falls the first grumpy little raindrop.
{name} plops down in the grass and frowns at the whole forest. The cloud is as big as a pillow now, and something inside it rumbles — quietly, but very crossly. What now?
Just then Granny Badger comes down the path with a basket of sweet-smelling herbs. She looks at the cloud and isn't surprised one bit. "Well, well," she says gently, "I know that cloud."
"That's anger," Granny explains. "It visits everyone. It even visits me." {name} blinks in surprise — does Granny really get a cloud like this too? "Oh yes, and an even bigger one!" she laughs.
"If you shout at anger, it grows. If you hide, it follows. But I know a secret..." And Granny picks a fluffy white dandelion.

"Watch. Breathe in through your nose, slowly, like you're smelling a flower. Now blow on the dandelion, soft and slow and long, so the fluff floats away gently." The seeds drift through the air like tiny parasols.
{name} holds the dandelion in both paws. In through the nose — like smelling a flower. Then a long, slow breath out: whoooosh... The fluff sails away, soft and easy.
The cloud overhead turns lighter! It was dark — now it's soft grey, like a little mouse. "One more time," smiles Granny Badger.
{name} breathes in through the nose again and lets the air out slowly: whoooosh... The cloud shrinks smaller and smaller, and turns white and soft as dandelion fluff.
The third breath is the slowest of all. The cloud turns tiny and gentle, and the breeze carries it away over the old oak. {name} waves a paw: bye-bye, little cloud!
"You see," says Granny, "anger fades when you don't feed it — not with shouting, not with stomping. Breathe slowly, and off it goes." {name} nods happily.
Then they build the tower together, and Granny passes the pebbles one by one. It stands! And when one pebble tumbles off after all, {name} just blows slowly — whoooosh — and bursts out laughing.

The sun settles behind the old oak, and the clearing smells of dandelions. {name} sits by the burrow and blows on one last dandelion, just for the joy of it. Because now {name} knows the secret: breathe slowly, and any grumpy cloud will float away.
